_doc: Crafting's numbers (docs/CRAFTING_DESIGN.md). Index by rarity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Storied. Temper's steps are to grade II, III, IV; remake's to Uncommon, Rare, Epic.
_brews: Wenna's draughts: cheaper than Harlan's (a health draught is 15 there), never stronger. The moonpetal draught (60%) has combat's yes.
_commission: Brannoc's 'make me one': Uncommon, the material's affix at grade I, full heat, ready the next morning. Gold is what the piece would fetch.
_bind: Vonnra's binding (design 7.3): a shard and 40 gold a grade bound; the piece that takes it spends 5-7 heat; the donor is unmade.
_mark: Marks (design 20.3): a map's ruler leaves its people's thing with its Mark, at a grade every three tiers (sometimes one finer); Vonnra inscribes it in a seam. Worn three at once, in the maps only.
_shelves: Rook's storeroom by shelves of 24 (the owner's approval): one with the room; the next cost these, then 'then' each, to 'most'. Her prices follow how she feels about you.
_charts: Working charts at the Wayfinder's table (design 20.4): a chart's heat by rarity (plain, fine, rare); ink a side, burn and redraw, pin, scrape, annotate. Shards from the scars, the people's material and iron from the atlas.
_slurry: Snib's jars (design 9), while the pump runs: 30 gold, three a day. Steeping, by weight: a grade past the cap, a slurry affix past the seams, only the veins, a grade lost. It sets the piece.
_crafters: Conversations hold the words said in them: Brannoc's fang node, Maeca's braid (dialogue.json, maeca: shed_fur_offer, shed_fur_braid) and her fang.seen (a once-only 'said' in npcs.json). Here are the lines said at a bench and written on what is made.

brannoc.name: Brannoc
brannoc.closedLine: Forge is banked. Come back by day.

greet: Dry day. Iron'll take the heat.
first.workIn: What it came off, it guards against. Old rule.
first.cage.before: The coal takes a long time to go dark in its cage. When it does, it is the shape of a thumbprint.
first.cage.after: His eyes go to the two irons on his rack, and come back.
first.remake: Old iron's good iron. Just tired.
first.rekindle: Heat comes back. Costs more each time. Like anything.
history.cage: A coal from {night}, caged by {who}, day {day}
fang.set: Set. It'll bite for you now.
history.fang: Set with Greymuzzle's fang on Brannoc's anvil, day {day}
history.commission: Made for you on Brannoc's anvil, day {day}

easier.line: He takes his time over it.
He has iron to spare for you.

history.shedFur: Braided by Maeca from what the Pack shed, day {day}

vonnra.name: Vonnra
vonnra.closedLine: Pay the toll first. Then we shall see what else you can afford.

greet: Put them on the table. The one you would keep, and the one you would give up for it.
Sit. The lamp is lit. It is always lit.
Two things on my table, and only one goes home with you. Choose.
first.bind.before: She holds the old piece above the lamp's chimney, in the heat and out of the flame, and waits with her eyes on the road. It takes a long time. Then something goes out of it, the way a held breath goes, and she lays the piece you are keeping in its place.
first.bind: There. It let go. Everything does, if one is patient with the lamp. ...It has somewhere to be now. That is all anything wants.
first.bind.after: What is left of the old piece is only metal. She sweeps it into the drawer with the day's tolls.
bind: It held. Things do, when they are told where.
Bound. It will not go back. It does not remember the way.
bind.caged: That one is in Brannoc's cage. He makes a good cage. It stays where he put it.
first.mark: Marked. It will do it that way now, until it breaks.
mark: It has its mark. It will keep it.

easier.line: She charges you a tenth less. She does not say why.

wayfinder.name: Ysolde
wayfinder.closedLine: I don't put my pen to a stranger's chart. Come and be introduced.

greet: Lay it flat, and your elbows off it. That ink's still deciding.
Back from the edges? Show me where you've been.
Sit. Mind the pens. What's the ground been saying?
first.ink.before: She takes a pen from the jar without looking, dips it, and writes in the margin in a hand too small to read upside down.
first.ink: There. Sworn. I don't choose the words, mind; the ground does. I only hold the pen.
ink: There. The ground's had its say.
Written. It'll pay for that, one way or the other.
first.burn.before: She holds the margin to the lamp until the oaths in it brown and lift, brushes them off like crumbs, and writes it fresh.
first.burn: Same ground, new oaths. The ground doesn't remember what it swore last time. Neither do I, much.
burn: Ask again if you don't like it. I'm paid either way.
first.pin.before: She threads a scrap of what that ground gave you onto a long brass pin, and puts it through the margin beside the oath, the way you'd pin a moth.
first.pin: Pinned. That one stays put when the rest go up. ...Everybody's got one of those.
pin: Held. Burn round it all you like.
first.scrape.before: She takes a penknife to the margin and scrapes the oath off a little at a time, the way a clerk takes out a name that shouldn't be in the ledger.
first.scrape: Gone. It never quite goes, mind. Hold it to the light and you'll still see where it was.
first.annotate.before: She lays the two charts side by side and copies from one to the other in a hand as small as stitching: who went in, where they lay up, what they carried out.
first.annotate: Two charts of the one ground are worth more than twice one. People leave things out. ...I put them back in.
first.annotate.after: The chart you gave up goes into a drawer, not the fire. She locks the drawer.
annotate: Margins full. That's how I like them.
Nothing wasted. I'm a tidy woman.
history.ink: Sworn in the Wayfinder's hand, day {day}
history.burn: Burned and redrawn at {who}'s table, day {day}
history.pin: An oath pinned at {who}'s table, day {day}
history.scrape: An oath scraped out by {who}, day {day}
history.annotate: Annotated from another chart in {who}'s hand, day {day}

snib.name: Snib
snib.closedLine: No slurry, no jars. Snib is VERY sad about it. Snib is not sad about it.

greet: Jars! Slurry jars! Three a day, Boss's orders. Boss did not order it. Snib is ordering it.
Snib does not SELL slurry. Snib sells JARS. The slurry is free. ...It is thirty gold.
You again. Snib has jars. Do not open them indoors.
jar: It is the GOOD stuff. Snib would not drink it. Snib would not drink the bad stuff EITHER.
jar.sale: Thirty. Snib does not haggle. Snib haggles. Thirty.
jar.none: No more today. Pump needs its sleep. Pump does not sleep.
steep.up: The veins take, and the iron drinks. It stays warm in your hand for a long time after.
steep.affix: Something green settles in it and stays. It is never quite still after.
steep.down: It hisses. Something in it gives.
first.steep.before: He takes the lid off at arm's length and looks away. What is in the jar is the colour of the stream below the pipe, and warm. The piece goes in, and something in the jar moves to meet it.
first.steep: There! Steeped! Snib did not see it move. It did not move.
steep.bad: That is not Snib's fault. That is the JAR's fault. ...Snib filled the jar.
steep: Steeped. Snib would not wear that. Snib would. Snib cannot afford it.
Green. GREEN. That is the good green. That is the bad green. Same green.
Do not lick it. Snib licked it once. Snib got promoted.
history.steep: Steeped in one of Snib's jars, day {day}

workIn.line: I've half the Verge coughing, child. Bring me a clean stream and I'll stitch your coat.

greet: Sit. Not there— that's Tam's chest-rub. What is it, child?
Kettle's on, still's not. Quick, child.
Bitterroot, moonpetal, and mind the shelf— it's older than you.
brew: Bitterroot, boiled twice. Hold your nose.
Drink it cold. It's worse, and it works.
brew.antidote: Antidote. You won't need it till you do.
first.brew: Bitter's the point, child— the body hates it, and gets up to get away from it. Drink.
brew.moonpetal: Moonpetal. Opens at night, shuts at dawn— like some I could name. Drink it cold.
flask.sale: A flask. Pewter, a lid that fits, my mark on the bottom. Rook fills it every night you sleep under her roof. A hundred and twenty, and it's cheap.
flask.filled: Rook has filled Wenna's flask by the fire: {n} draughts. The bitterroot's gone into it.
flask.dry: Wenna's flask is dry, and there's no bitterroot to fill it. Rook shakes it at you on your way past.
first.workIn: There. Bitterroot in the lining— don't pick at it— keeps your blood where it belongs. Off you go, child.
workIn: In it goes. Smells foul; works.

easier.line: She takes more care over yours.
